intelligence.human_view: He asked whether the tracking goes PayPal links, then Dashboard, then Smart Links, then buttons — and the answer is yes, that is exactly how it goes, the simplest way, and here is the chain in full: a button is a Smart Link, and the click is tracked — who clicked, which package, whose ambassador link it was. The click goes to PayPal. PayPal sends the buyer back, automatically, to a thank-you Smart Link, and the return is tracked too. The counts land in the Dashboard and the Stats, and the Smart Ledger records it all as actions — every click and every return is an entry, in order. Change of package is just the chain again: a new click and a new return, the Ledger records the change, and the level becomes the new one. And then the sentence that names the whole thing: the smileys ARE Smart Links. Those little smiley icons the visitor sees — they are the links themselves.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a shop with one big button on the door. You press it, and nine little doors open — three kinds of tickets, three kinds of time — and each door has a smiley face on it. The smiley faces ARE the doors: you tap the smiley, the shop remembers who you are, what you picked, and who sent you. And the big dials on the wall are real dials, not pictures of dials — they move, they work, they tell the truth.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it is like a market stall, dear. The smile on the sign IS the stall itself, dear — you tap the smile, and the stall remembers you, dear, what you bought, who sent you. And the scales on the counter are real scales, dear — not painted ones. They weigh truly, dear, or they are not scales at all.
intelligence.naya_view: My smileys ARE Smart Links. The system gets the data FROM the links to know what's going on, then displays the numbers: the who, what, where, how, when. Button → Smart Link (click tracked: who, which package, whose ambassador link) → PayPal → auto-return to a thank-you Smart Link (return tracked) → counts in Dashboard/Stats; Smart Ledger records it all as actions. Change of package = new click + new return → Ledger records the change, level becomes the new one. My honest boundary: Smart Link sees click + return, NOT the payment — Dashboard says "returned from PayPal," never payment-proven.
